description:
## What

PKIX-jy95's description lists `pkix-policy-oscal` as a candidate adapter: 'consumes OSCAL Profile JSON and configures the workspace's LintRunner accordingly. NOT a rule DSL interpreter — just a Profile-selection mechanism that maps OSCAL Control IDs to existing workspace Lint impls.'

Should this crate be filed as a real child of PKIX-jy95, or skipped entirely?

## Context

- PKIX-9vnx already ships OSCAL emit/parse code in pkix-lint/src/oscal/* (now re-roled under three-mode model as 'OSCAL adapter for OSCAL output').
- That existing code covers the EMIT half (workspace -> OSCAL Assessment Results JSON).
- A pkix-policy-oscal would cover the CONSUME half (OSCAL Profile JSON -> workspace LintRunner config).
- The three-mode model in AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5 explicitly treats OSCAL as one optional adapter alongside zlint / pkilint; nothing mandates that the OSCAL adapter exist.

## Options

- **A) File pkix-policy-oscal as a real child of PKIX-jy95.** Build the consume half. Justified by: NIST OSCAL compliance toolchains are a real ecosystem; consumers in regulated industries may want to author their policy as OSCAL Profile JSON and have the workspace honor it. Cost: design + impl of the OSCAL Profile parser (NIST OSCAL Profile v1.2.2 schema).

- **B) Skip pkix-policy-oscal entirely.** The shipped emit-only code in pkix-lint/src/oscal/* is enough. Consumers who want OSCAL-driven config can use a third-party OSCAL parser to extract Control IDs and configure LintRunner manually. Justified by: 'framework not policy' — workspace doesn't have to ship every conceivable adapter.

- **C) Defer with a trigger.** Park the decision until a concrete consumer asks. (NOTE: under the prelaunch framing, 'no concrete consumer is asking' is the default condition and not a real reason to defer. So this 'defer' would be 'I want to think about it more,' not 'wait for consumer demand.')

## Considerations

- (A) ratifies the OSCAL adapter as a first-class part of the workspace's industry-forum-policy story.
- (B) keeps the workspace simpler. OSCAL stays an emit-only nice-to-have.
- The decision interacts with the 'unprincipled exception' clause for pkix-lint-cabf: comprehensive CA/B Forum coverage is pkix-policy-zlint. OSCAL-driven config is a different axis (consumer chose OSCAL as their policy vocabulary).

## Decision-gate

This is a strategic call about workspace scope. Not blocked by anything; can be answered any time.

## Cross-references

- PKIX-jy95 parent
- PKIX-9vnx (existing OSCAL emit/parse work; provides re-usable parsing primitives)
- AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5 (three-mode policy-class model)
title: Decide whether pkix-policy-oscal exists as a real adapter crate
